Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after potentially damaging marital affairs
After multiple legally-compromising affairs came to light in the public, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has tendered his resignation as the head of one of the largest companies in the world.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 12, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via NVIDIA/Anderseidesvik
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, has resigned as the CEO after scandals that rocked not only Huang's personal life but might be legally treacherous rock the company. An interim CEO, CFO Colette Kress, has been put in place by the company's board while Nvidia strategizes on a transition plan to appoint a permanent replacement.
In
a statement from Nvidia's board of directors
, the board confirms that Huang has resigned as president effectively immediately, and that the board is considering internal and external candidates to replace him.
The 63-year-old Huang resigned after Nvidia's board and the United States FBI launched an investigation into the CEO following his admission of an affair with a woman both groups believed to be a spy from China. That story, which Huang appeared to choose to weather from his leadership position, was stacked upon this week by reporting by the
New York Times
alleging a second affair between Huang and a subordinate executive at Nvidia.

The situation puts Huang in a dicey legal area. The first woman he was accused of having an affair with, Alice Huang—no familial relation with Jensen Huang—is a Chinese national and former executive of a Singapore-based cloud computing company named Megaspeed. The United State intelligence community, according to the FBI investigation into Huang and confirmed by Treasure Secretary Scott Bessent, has long suspected Megaspeed of diverting its purchased chips from Nvidia to China.
These national security concerns were reportedly expressed to the US president ahead of a recent China trip, roughly coinciding with the time that President Trump asked the Department of Commerce to carve out exceptions to export restrictions to sell AI chips to Chinese buyers, on the condition that the United States government collects on a 25 percent tariff for each sale.
Nvidia is
the first publicly-traded company to reach a $5.5 trillion market capitalization value
, making it not only the largest company in the gaming and tech industry, but one of the largest companies in the world. Nvidia tech powers both Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 and
holds about 95% of the consumer GPU market
. The company is also the tip of the spear in supercomputing and AI technologies,
supplying roughly 75% of all the GPUs to AI data centers
.
Upheaval or chaos in Nvidia is likely to have far-reaching complications for the entire industry and arguably global economies.
